name: Srivilliputhur Andal Temple (Vatapatrasayi)
deity: Vishnu as Vatapatrasayi, reclining on the banyan leaf, with Andal (Kodhai Nachiyar), the only woman among the Alvar saints
period: A Divya Desam of the Pandya country, and the shrine of Andal, whose Thiruppavai is sung across the Tamil month of Margazhi
summary: At Srivilliputhur, Vishnu reclines as Vatapatrasayi beside the shrine of Andal — the girl-saint who loved him as her bridegroom. Its towering rajagopuram is the emblem of Tamil Nadu, and its Thiruppavai is sung through the whole month of Margazhi.

sections.history: Srivilliputhur, in the Pandya country of southern Tamil Nadu, is honoured as the home of Andal — Kodhai, the only woman among the twelve Alvar saints. Tradition holds that Periyalvar, her foster father, found her as an infant beneath a tulsi plant in the temple garden, and that she grew up loving Vishnu so wholly that she wore the garlands meant for him and would take no other bridegroom. The temple is a Divya Desam, one of the 108 abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars, and its presiding lord is Vatapatrasayi, worshipped alongside Andal in her own celebrated shrine.
sections.architecture: Built in the Dravidian manner and enlarged under later patrons, the temple is crowned by a soaring eleven-tiered rajagopuram, one of the tallest in the land — so emblematic that it is the official emblem of the Government of Tamil Nadu. Within, the lord Vatapatrasayi reclines upon the serpent, while Andal is enshrined in her adjoining temple; pillared halls and painted ceilings carry the devotional art of the deep south.
sections.legends: Andal's love is the temple's living legend: she is said to have offered Vishnu garlands she had first worn herself, and her Thiruppavai and Nachiyar Tirumozhi remain among the most beloved of Tamil devotional poems. In the end, tradition tells, she was united with Ranganatha of Srirangam and merged into the lord — the only Alvar, and the only woman, to be so wedded to the divine. Her festival marriage to Ranganatha is re-enacted here each year.
sections.festivals: The month of Margazhi belongs to Andal, when her Thiruppavai is chanted daily in homes and temples across the Tamil country. Aadi Pooram, celebrating her appearance, and the festival of her wedding to Ranganatha draw great crowds, with processions through the temple town beneath its great tower.
sections.experience: To stand before Andal's shrine is to enter one of the most intimate devotions in the Tamil tradition — a saint who is also a bride. Pilgrims come for the Thiruppavai season and for the sight of the rajagopuram rising over the town, a landmark carried on the emblem of the state itself.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Margazhi month and Aadi Pooram are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Srivilliputhur lies in Virudhunagar district of southern Tamil Nadu, off the Madurai–Sivakasi road, reachable by road and rail; Madurai is the nearest major hub and airport.
